title: He was ready to split the baby.
paragraphs: He was ready to split the baby.
That’s how far a broken heart will go when pride takes over.
the real mother was willing to lose everything… just to save the child.
And that’s where the story stops being ancient…
God will allow a moment that looks like destruction—
just to reveal what love really is.
Not every “love” we claim is actually love.
Some of it is fear dressed up as affection.
“If I can’t have it… no one will.”
That’s the human heart without surrender.
It would rather destroy something beautiful than admit it’s wrong.
How many relationships have been cut in half because no one wanted to humble themselves?
How many words have been like swords?
How many moments where you chose to be right…
“Please, my lord, give her the living child! Do not kill him!”
And here’s the lesson that will wreck you if you let it:
Real love is proven by what it’s willing to release—not what it fights to control.
“Even if it costs me… let life win.”
Because this story doesn’t end in Solomon’s court.
It points to a greater moment.
Another innocent life stood in judgment.
but between a holy God and a sinful world.
no one stepped forward to stop the sword.
Because we were the guilty ones.

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
(Romans 3:23)
He didn’t fight for His rights.

“He was pierced for our transgressions… crushed for our iniquities.”
(Isaiah 53:5)
so you wouldn’t have to be destroyed by your sin.
That’s the kind of love that doesn’t just feel—
And now the question turns back to you.
Where is pride still speaking in your life?
Even if it costs someone else?
Even if it destroys something God is trying to heal?
Because the sword is still revealing hearts today.

“For the word of God is alive and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword…”
(Hebrews 4:12)
The hidden sin you’ve been protecting.
The version of “love” that’s really just fear.
Because only He can take a divided heart—
Only He can turn pride into surrender.
Only He can turn shame into redemption.
If this stirred something deep in you…
